what: OGE Energy owns Oklahoma Gas and Electric, the regulated utility that supplies electricity to most of Oklahoma and part of western Arkansas. Rates are set by state regulators.
customers: Households and businesses in Oklahoma and western Arkansas, who have no alternative supplier.
moat: A legal monopoly over electricity in its territory, earning a regulated return on everything it invests in the network.
risks: $5.4B of debt against essentially no cash
The analyst average target is right where the shares trade
Oklahoma regulators set the allowed return, and a poor decision lasts for years
opportunities: A 14.4% net margin guaranteed by the regulated structure
Data centre development in Oklahoma is lifting electricity demand after years of flat load
Revenue grew from $2.7B to $3.3B in two years
watch: Load growth from new large customers and rate case outcomes.
